auditor: separate-model review (three independent Claude Opus agents, one pass, read-only)

The baseline review was a single pass. Follow-up evidence and review heads are recorded on individual re-audited entries.
One receipt (radar_laser.radar L) received no verdict and was not promoted.
Reviewers could run the cited tests; they did not review the engines line by line.

RCP-force_platform-dual-A.reason: The dual-specific refusals are real: timebase, legacy shared-clock and unrelated-acquisition. No vendor/native-stage (adapter) or non-finite refusal is tested.

RCP-force_platform-dual-B.fix: Cite/add dual invalid-calibration and contradictory-geometry refusal tests.
RCP-force_platform-dual-B.reason: Per-plate zeroing, the matrix and non-coplanar COP retention are exact. None of the cited tests checks a refusal of missing or contradictory calibration; test_invalid_calibration_rejects is not cited and runs single.

RCP-force_platform-dual-C.reason: test_dual_clock_mapping_and_explicit_overlap_resampling applies offset, drift and latency exactly at 1e-10 and refuses mismatched grids. Unknown reference clock and bad timebase are refused on dual fixtures.

RCP-force_platform-dual-D.reason: On dual fixtures, the clean noisy control is not rejected. Wrong side assignment fails FP-ASSIGN, step-off is refused, and isolated-load crosstalk fails FP-CROSSTALK-1. Parameter refusals are also covered.

RCP-force_platform-dual-E.fix: Record 0.15 m/s / 0.1 m; assert sensitivity output.
RCP-force_platform-dual-E.reason: Same variant matrix as single, parametrized over dual. The asserted bounds are 0.075-0.15 m/s and 0.1 m, while the receipt records 1e-9. No variant sensitivity is reported.

RCP-force_platform-dual-F.prior_reason: The dual reconstruction against the closed form is real, but the asserted bounds are 0.06 m/s and 0.07 m, against a recorded tolerance of 1e-10.
RCP-force_platform-dual-F.reason: The independent closed form matches production dual-plate reconstruction within both unit-specific bounds, including the accepted nonflat trials. Exact-flat trajectories also exercise diagnostic reconstruction.

RCP-force_platform-dual-G.fix: Run dual export through process()->JumpSignal->assess for CMJ events and bilateral split.
RCP-force_platform-dual-G.reason: Every jump_assessment fixture is force_platform.single (_signal). The bilateral and single-leg tests fake two plates with replace(plate_force_n=0.4/0.6 split) instead of running dual engine output.

RCP-force_platform-dual-H.fix: Add dual-fixture definition test incl. bilateral asymmetry, bound to registry claims.
RCP-force_platform-dual-H.reason: All three cited tests use single fixtures. Dual-specific bilateral metric definitions are not cited, and there is no registry-claim binding.

RCP-force_platform-dual-I.fix: Dual-fixture test: per-plate calibration bounds propagate to envelope matching closed form.
RCP-force_platform-dual-I.reason: The three cited tests (conditional uncertainty, filtered envelopes, threshold sensitivity) all run force_platform.single. Two-plate uncertainty combination is never exercised or compared with an analytic value.

RCP-force_platform-dual-J.prior_reason: The reference is independent, and the reconstruction test covers dual against the closed form. The recorded 1e-10 comes from engine-internal and metamorphic checks; the reference comparison is at 0.06/0.07.
RCP-force_platform-dual-J.reason: The independent closed form matches production dual-plate reconstruction within both unit-specific bounds, including the accepted nonflat trials. Exact-flat trajectories also exercise diagnostic reconstruction.

RCP-force_platform-dual-K.fix: Parametrize remaining continuous/protocol fault classes on dual export with expected verdicts.

RCP-force_platform-dual-M.reason: The same provenance test is parametrized for dual (2 plates, two input digests), with change detection on fz_left. The 'source sha == [x] or len==plates' assertion is slightly loose.

RCP-force_platform-single-B.fix: Cite test_invalid_calibration_rejects and metadata-frame rejection in B; add single-plate zero-window test.
RCP-force_platform-single-B.reason: Matrix, rotation, origin and tilted-COP application are exact at 1e-12 against closed forms. None of the cited tests checks a refusal, and the zeroing test uses a dual export.

RCP-force_platform-single-C.fix: Add single-plate test: declared latency/clock offset shifts time_s exactly; cite it.
RCP-force_platform-single-C.reason: The only cited test, test_bad_timebase_rejects, runs a dual fixture and checks refusal only. No test applies latency_s or clock offset/drift to a single plate (force_platform_acquisition.py:171-190).

RCP-force_platform-single-E.fix: Record tolerance 0.15 m/s / 0.1 m; assert reported inter-variant sensitivity.

RCP-force_platform-single-F.prior_reason: test_reconstructs_all_vertical_fixtures runs single and dual against the Trajectory closed form, but the asserted bounds are 0.06 m/s and 0.07 m, against a recorded tolerance of 1e-10, which overstates precision by roughly 9 orders of magnitude.
RCP-force_platform-single-F.reason: The independent closed form matches production single-plate reconstruction within both unit-specific bounds, including the accepted nonflat trials. Exact-flat trajectories also exercise diagnostic reconstruction.

RCP-force_platform-single-G.reason: CMJ, SJ, DJ and hops events and phases match closed forms within 2-3 samples on single fixtures. Eligibility refusals are present: SJ/CMJ cross-check, no flight, too few hops and no onset. The 0.01 tolerance is consistent.

RCP-force_platform-single-I.fix: Assert envelope equals the closed form for declared bounds; make the receipt numeric.

RCP-force_platform-single-J.prior_reason: The reference is genuinely independent (kinematics.py imports only stdlib, and the import-boundary test passes). RCP-force_platform-single-J.reason: The independent closed form matches production single-plate reconstruction within both unit-specific bounds, including the accepted nonflat trials. Exact-flat trajectories also exercise diagnostic reconstruction.

RCP-force_platform-single-K.fix: Parametrize OFFSET/CLIPPING/DROP/STEP_OFF on single export with expected process() verdicts.

RCP-force_platform-single-L.reason: Flight-time studies run the single-plate engine against contact and IMU engines and are classified. All 12 studies claim no interchangeability, and rejected trials are diagnostic-only. Asserted bias bounds reach 0.006, not the recorded 0.002.

RCP-force_platform-single-M.reason: The test round-trips a file and checks that the report reproduces exactly, records the source sha, input digests and QC-rules hash, and changes digest when the input changes. Exporter determinism and tamper rejection are also cited.

RCP-gnss_lps-gnss-A.reason: GNSS: 9 contradictory declarations (rate, stage, latency, drift, bundle, ENU, Doppler) and resampled provenance are refused, and positive admission is exact. The missing-time and truth-input refusals are LPS-only but share the code path.

RCP-gnss_lps-gnss-B.fix: Cite the enu_origin=None case and add contradictory geometry or antenna-offset refusals.
RCP-gnss_lps-gnss-B.reason: The ENU equator closed form at 4e-9 is good. test_single_bad_gnss_sample_refuses is QC, not calibration or geometry. The missing ENU-origin refusal sits in an uncited test, and no antenna or lever-arm record is exercised.

RCP-gnss_lps-gnss-C.reason: For GNSS, latency and −160 ppm drift are mapped to truth at 1e-12, and drift without bracketing sync pulses is refused. Jitter refusal for five_point is shown on LPS (shared engine). The tolerance matches.

RCP-gnss_lps-gnss-D.prior_reason: Refusals are strong: res669 dropout/jump/interpolation plus satellites, HDOP, fix, multipath and signal integrity. But neither cited test includes a clean-control pass.
RCP-gnss_lps-gnss-D.reason: The GNSS clean control and position-mutation cases execute against the named subfamily. The remaining cited controls verify refusal for invalid satellites, HDOP, fix quality, multipath, signal flag and Doppler.

RCP-gnss_lps-gnss-E.fix: Parametrize the E tests over gnss and compare each variant with the GeodeticTrack truth.
RCP-gnss_lps-gnss-E.reason: All three cited tests (three_point/five_point jitter, seeded-noise sensitivity, five_point rate-unavailable) run track_case('lps') only. No GNSS variant is exercised, and sensitivity is not compared with a reference.

RCP-gnss_lps-gnss-F.reason: test_closed_form_acceleration_speed_distance_and_doppler[gnss] checks position, speed, acceleration and distance against t+t² closed forms for both derivatives. Bounds of 4e-9 to 1e-5 are consistent.

RCP-gnss_lps-gnss-G.reason: The GNSS Doppler threshold test recovers exact run counts, durations and integrated distances, and refuses the single-sample run. The 1e-5 tolerance comes from the closed-form test. Events are exact.

RCP-gnss_lps-gnss-H.fix: Add a registry-binding assertion once RES-694 lands.
RCP-gnss_lps-gnss-H.reason: Doppler and positional estimands are kept separate and executed exactly. But no cited test binds the metrics to sourced registry claims, and the docs say GNSS registry claims are absent (RES-694).

RCP-gnss_lps-gnss-I.fix: Propagate a GNSS position σ to speed and acceleration and compare with the closed-form variance.
RCP-gnss_lps-gnss-I.reason: Both cited tests are LPS-only. They check sensitivity inequalities or absence and make no analytical uncertainty comparison.

RCP-gnss_lps-gnss-J.fix: Add an AST no-reference-import test for gnss_lps engines.
RCP-gnss_lps-gnss-J.reason: The engine matches the independent closed form (ENU equator, t+t² track). The reference geodetic_ecef is checked against the PROJ published example at 1 mm. The engine imports no reference code (verified by grep), though no cited test checks this.

RCP-gnss_lps-gnss-K.reason: The inject outputs (jump in metres, dropout, interpolation, seeded noise) are verified against independent closed forms and are deterministic. test_res669 asserts engine refusal verdicts for each class on GNSS.

RCP-gnss_lps-gnss-L.reason: radar_vs_positional_speed (radar vs gnss) latency bias matches the closed form at rel 1e-9 and is classified definition_mismatch, with no interchangeability claims. The recorded 0.001 comes from a != assertion. It is conservative but mis-extracted.

RCP-gnss_lps-gnss-M.prior_fix: Round-trip through io.write/read, assert a non-None data_sha256 equal to the file hash, and assert that the digest changes on mutation.
RCP-gnss_lps-gnss-M.prior_reason: test_track_results_record_acquisition_hashes asserts 'data_sha256 == meta sha OR None'. A probe shows both are None for gnss, so the result is not hash-bound. There is no file round-trip and no input-change detection.
RCP-gnss_lps-gnss-M.reason: File-backed GNSS processing records the verified synthetic observation hash and deterministically replays the seeded export, declaration and processing result. Exact outcomes: independent seed-700 regeneration gives identical Parquet, sidecar and processing report bytes. The acquisition digest equals the independently hashed Parquet, changes after a 0.005 m sample mutation, and tampering results in an input integrity refusal.

RCP-gnss_lps-gnss-O.fix: Bind the limitations to sourced records.
RCP-gnss_lps-gnss-O.reason: The heuristic limitation test [gnss] checks no sourcing, for a single configuration.

RCP-gnss_lps-lps-A.prior_fix: Parametrize the contradictory and resampling tests over lps.
RCP-gnss_lps-lps-A.prior_reason: The contradictory-declaration and resampled-provenance refusals are GNSS-only. LPS refusals cover only missing or duplicate time and the truth input. No stage or vendor refusal is tested on LPS.
RCP-gnss_lps-lps-A.reason: LPS admission accepts the intact native observation and verifies stage, geometry declarations, units and native data integrity. Exact outcomes: refuse processed and resampled stages, noncanonical centimetres, contradictory rate/uncertainty/latency/drift/identity, missing or duplicate timestamps, and analytical truth supplied as an observation.

RCP-gnss_lps-lps-B.prior_reason: The anchor geometry and Z-up frame refusals are good. But no cited test shows the anchor geometry or frame being applied exactly (positional exactness is in an uncited test). Recorded categorical.
RCP-gnss_lps-lps-B.reason: The native LPS control returns the closed-form Z-up XYZ and its surveyed anchors. Explicit frame and anchor checks refuse unknown, duplicate or collinear declarations and missing or occluded anchors.

RCP-gnss_lps-lps-C.prior_fix: Parametrize the sync-pulse refusal over lps.
RCP-gnss_lps-lps-C.prior_reason: LPS latency and +120 ppm drift are exact at 1e-12, and duplicate time and jitter are refused. But the bracketing sync-pulse drift refusal (test_drift_needs_bracketing_sync_pulses) runs GNSS only.
RCP-gnss_lps-lps-C.reason: LPS maps declared time using a bracketing affine clock and latency model, retains timing uncertainty and refuses unresolved drift. Measurement time is (1−160e−6)k/25 seconds and reference receipt time adds 0.038 s. Both arrays use absolute 1e-12 s with zero relative tolerance, allowing round-off only. Alignment and latency uncertainties are 1e-12 and 0.001 s. Unbracketed drift and unsupported jitter are refused.

RCP-gnss_lps-lps-D.prior_fix: Cite a clean LPS admission control.
RCP-gnss_lps-lps-D.prior_reason: On LPS, dropout, jump, interpolation, occlusion and degenerate anchors are refused. Neither cited test includes a clean-control pass.
RCP-gnss_lps-lps-D.reason: The LPS clean control and position-mutation cases execute against the named subfamily. The remaining cited controls verify refusal for occlusion, missing visibility declaration and duplicate, collinear or unknown anchors.

RCP-gnss_lps-lps-E.prior_fix: Compare five_point and binomial5 against the PlanarTrajectory truth with stated bounds.
RCP-gnss_lps-lps-E.prior_reason: three_point is checked exactly on jittered LPS. The binomial5 and every-second-sample variants assert only inequalities, and five_point appears only as a refusal or retention. No reference comparison exists for those variants. Recorded categorical despite numeric asserts.
RCP-gnss_lps-lps-E.reason: LPS three-point and five-point differentiation, all three position smoothers and reported alternate-filter and half-rate effects agree with independent linear and quadratic controls. For x=0.75t, speed and acceleration are 0.75 m/s and zero. For x=t+t², interior filter shifts are μ₂h² for μ₂=0,2,1 and speed/acceleration are 1+2t and 2. At the common 2.96 s endpoint, quadratic velocity peaks are 6.92−h(3w₁+5w₂); three-point acceleration peaks are 2 and five-point peaks are 2, 2+1/30 and 2+17/576 m/s² for none, boxcar and binomial. Sample times use 1e-12 s, rate 1e-9 Hz, position and speed 2e-12 in their units and acceleration 2e-10 m/s² to allow differentiation round-off, all with zero relative tolerance.

RCP-gnss_lps-lps-F.reason: The closed-form tests [lps] and the turning-point test check speed, vector acceleration (−2cos t) and chord distance against PlanarTrajectory within the 1e-5 bound.

RCP-gnss_lps-lps-G.prior_fix: Add an LPS horizontal_positional_speed threshold test with analytically known run times and dwell refusals.
RCP-gnss_lps-lps-G.prior_reason: test_doppler_threshold_counts... runs track_case('gnss') on Doppler. For LPS (no Doppler) nothing checks positional-speed threshold runs or events against known times.
RCP-gnss_lps-lps-G.reason: LPS horizontal positional speed qualification retains the known sampled above-threshold interval with exact run counts and refuses under-dwell or isolated samples. At 25 Hz, v=1+2t first exceeds 3.01 m/s at 1.04 s. The final row is 3 s, so the retained interval is 1.96 s and x(3)−x(1.04)=9.8784 m. Absolute rounding allowances are 1e-12 s and 2e-12 m. Dwell of 1.97 s and the isolated ≥6.99 m/s row both give zero runs and zero totals.

RCP-gnss_lps-lps-H.fix: Add an LPS-specific estimand and registry-binding assertion.
RCP-gnss_lps-lps-H.reason: LPS estimand separation and execution are exact. test_doppler_and_positional_speed_are_different_traces is GNSS-only. No registry binding is tested, and registry claims are absent (RES-694).

RCP-gnss_lps-lps-I.fix: Compare the propagated noise-to-derivative σ with the closed-form finite-difference variance.
RCP-gnss_lps-lps-I.reason: The cited tests assert only that sensitivity fields exist and that filtered acceleration < native. Neither compares the declared uncertainty with an independent analytical result.

RCP-gnss_lps-lps-J.prior_fix: Replace the geodetic citations with an LPS trilateration or planar closed-form test plus an import check.
RCP-gnss_lps-lps-J.prior_reason: The LPS closed-form test is genuine. The ENU equator and WGS84/PROJ tests are irrelevant to the planar LPS path, and no cited test checks the LPS engine's import independence.
RCP-gnss_lps-lps-J.reason: LPS native processing uses an independent planar motion and rigid-body oracle, and matches it without sharing production reconstruction code. On the quadratic track x=t+t² the interior smoothing adjustment is μ₂/25² with μ₂=0,2,1. Speed 1+2t and acceleration 2 agree at absolute 2e-12 m and m/s, and 2e-10 m/s², with zero relative tolerance. Linear and quadratic sensitivity use the rate, duration and boundary values detailed in RCP-gnss_lps-lps-E.

RCP-gnss_lps-lps-K.reason: Position faults on LPS are verified exactly against independent formulas and are deterministic. test_res669[lps] asserts refusal verdicts per class.

RCP-gnss_lps-lps-L.fix: Assert radar_vs_lps_speed sensitivities against the latency closed form.
RCP-gnss_lps-lps-L.reason: The radar_vs_lps_speed study exists, but no cited test checks it against a closed form. test_positional... checks the GNSS study, and the handoff test is GNSS-only. LPS is covered only by the generic counting test.

RCP-gnss_lps-lps-M.prior_fix: Use the same fix as gnss-M, parametrized for lps.
RCP-gnss_lps-lps-M.prior_reason: For lps, data_sha256 is also None (probe), so the hash assertion passes vacuously. The frozen-bytes test covers only the GNSS reference export, not LPS processing.
RCP-gnss_lps-lps-M.reason: File-backed LPS processing records the verified synthetic observation hash and deterministically replays the seeded export, declaration and processing result. Exact outcomes: independent seed-700 regeneration gives identical Parquet, sidecar and processing report bytes. The acquisition digest equals the independently hashed Parquet, changes after a 0.005 m sample mutation, and tampering results in an input integrity refusal.

RCP-gnss_lps-lps-O.fix: Bind the limitations to sourced records.
RCP-gnss_lps-lps-O.reason: The heuristic limitation test [lps] checks no sourcing.

RCP-imu-inertial-A.fix: Add stage, unit-label and non-finite or non-monotonic input refusals for imu.inertial.
RCP-imu-inertial-A.reason: Only the wrong device class and a missing gyro channel are refused. The integration refusal is a method precondition, not admission. No native/vendor stage, unit or integrity-refusal tests exist for IMU.

RCP-imu-inertial-B.reason: An independent forward model (scale, bias, misalignment) is inverted at 1e-9. Undeclared placement and non-invertible or improper matrices are refused. Static tilt recovers roll and pitch at 1e-9.

RCP-imu-inertial-D.reason: Gaps, saturation, spike, sync, rate, gyro-bias and slip each give FAIL or reject. Clean controls give PASS or NOT_APPLICABLE, and the slip magnitude matches at 1e-6.

RCP-imu-inertial-E.reason: All declared variants are covered: gyro_integration (bias·t), complementary (bias/gain), declared_initial_velocity, zupt_linear_drift, plus the unobservable refusal. Each has a closed form. Tolerance 0.01 matches the complementary bound.

RCP-imu-inertial-F.reason: Rotation at 1e-9 and free acceleration at 1e-8 against RigidBody truth. Trapezoid velocity and position are within the derived error bound. Specific force is kept distinct.

RCP-imu-inertial-G.fix: Record the event tolerance as 2/hz = 0.004 s.
RCP-imu-inertial-G.reason: Flight takeoff and duration match the trajectory within 2/hz (4 ms), and min-duration eligibility is refused. But the recorded tolerance of 1e-9 comes from the free-fall norm, overstating event-time precision.

RCP-imu-inertial-H.fix: Add a registry-binding check once the claims exist.
RCP-imu-inertial-H.reason: Specific force vs free acceleration and IMU vs force flight estimates are kept separate and labelled at 0.004. No binding to sourced registry claims is tested, and IMU registry claims are absent (RES-694).

RCP-imu-inertial-I.reason: velocity_error_bound equals the bias·t closed form, and the complementary tilt bound equals bias/gain within 0.01. Both compare reported uncertainty with an analytical result.

RCP-imu-inertial-J.reason: The engine matches the RigidBody closed form at 1e-8. An AST test confirms imu.py imports no reference code. The reference itself is validated by finite differences and the inversion identity.

RCP-imu-inertial-K.fix: Cite test_static_gyro_bias_and_slip_are_flagged and add a misalignment verdict.
RCP-imu-inertial-K.reason: Inject bias, misalignment and saturation are verified exactly. But engine verdicts are asserted only for saturation (and for gaps via manual slicing). Misalignment and bias fixtures get no engine verdict in the cited tests.

RCP-imu-inertial-L.reason: force_vs_imu_flight_time is analytical_model_agreement with bias<0.006, and there are no empirical claims. The recorded tolerance of 0.002 is mis-extracted: the IMU-relevant bound is 0.006.

RCP-imu-inertial-O.fix: Bind the limitations to sourced records.
RCP-imu-inertial-O.reason: The heuristic limitation test [imu] checks no sourcing.

RCP-load_cell_isometric-isometric_rig-C.fix: Rig-fixture timing refusal and alignment test.
RCP-load_cell_isometric-isometric_rig-C.reason: No cited test runs the isometric_rig fixture. As for load_cell, clock alignment and sync-uncertainty propagation are untested.

RCP-load_cell_isometric-isometric_rig-D.fix: Inject offset/clipping into isometric_rig export and assert verdicts.

Use absolute 1e-12 s and m and 1e-11 m/s with zero relative tolerance for arithmetic roundoff. Refuse unresolved transitions.
